evidence.summary: Adversarial probe over the full legal FP16 domain (random, full-exponent-range samples, exact and extreme cancellation, subnormal/signed-zero/extrema value grids, all-pairs combinations, axis-aligned denominators, ~1M rows total) found ZERO violations of the contract tolerance 1e-7 + 5e-7*|target|; the worst observed error ratio was 0.285 of tolerance; all outputs were finite, inputs were preserved, and output was a fresh FP32 [N,2] CUDA tensor. The kernel meets the componentwise accuracy requirement.

rationale: The FP32 pipeline (exact products, one rounding for each sum, div_rn) should give ~3-ulp relative error (~1.8e-7) vs the 5e-7 relative + 1e-7 absolute tolerance, but cancellation-heavy, subnormal, and extremal inputs are where the bound is tightest and where FP32 stores could deviate.

scope_evidence.summary: Requirement: abs(actual - target) <= 1e-7 + 5e-7 * abs(target) for EACH output component; EVERY combination of finite FP16 component values is legal, including signed zeros, subnormals and both extrema; every output must be finite; inputs must be preserved.

scope_rationale: The contract explicitly requires the componentwise tolerance abs(actual-target) <= 1e-7 + 5e-7*abs(target) over every combination of finite FP16 components including signed zeros, subnormals and extrema, so a tolerance violation on any legal input is a contract violation.
statement: The Triton FP32 intermediate pipeline violates the contract tolerance 1e-7 + 5e-7*abs(target) on some legal FP16 input (e.g. strong cancellation in the numerator, subnormal/extremal components).
